Static implementation review · 4 September 2026

LoomTV has a strong foundation. Finish the API migration next.

The desktop, server, mobile and TV work shows substantial investment. The most useful next phase is consistency across clients, reliable failure recovery and smaller modules.

Evidence and limits

This review examined server authorization, setup, filesystem containment, desktop IPC and library mutations, plus mobile API adapters and artwork controls. Type checking and lint passed in this review session. No tests, runtime playback checks or visual verification were performed. This is a targeted review, not an exhaustive claim that every bug has been found.

Visible means directly present in source. Inferred means the consequence follows from the inspected code. Needs verification identifies behavior that requires execution or fault injection.

Findings

1 · Medium · Visible · Implementation

Setup exposes library paths to viewers

Problem. The setup library GET route requires only library.read and returns raw roots. The root view spreads the saved root, including its filesystem path. Ordinary viewer responses therefore reveal server directory names that the regular library endpoint removes.

Why it matters. Require library.manage for setup folder details, or return the same redacted root DTO used by the regular endpoint. Verify that a viewer cannot retrieve absolute paths through either route.

Evidence. apps/server/src/public-api.js:999; apps/server/src/admin-service.js:869 and :1510.

2 · Medium · Visible · Implementation

Setup completion waits without a deadline

Problem. waitForSetupScan polls every 250 ms until the scan changes state. Setup completion awaits it without a deadline or disconnect cancellation. If scanning stalls, the request cannot complete and polling continues after the client leaves.

Why it matters. Return a job identifier and let the client poll scan status, or enforce a deadline and cancellation. Keep scanning progress and retry controls available if setup takes longer than expected.

Evidence. apps/server/src/public-api.js:460 and :1150. A stalled scan was not reproduced.

3 · Medium · Visible · Implementation

The poster-refresh control cannot succeed

Problem. The detail screen renders a refresh-poster button, and its handler calls getOfficialArtworkCandidates. That method always returns HTTP 410 with legacy_route_retired. Applying artwork is also hardcoded to fail.

Why it matters. Implement these operations through the canonical API or hide the controls until the server advertises support. A displayed action should have a supported success path.

Evidence. apps/mobile/App.tsx:2982 and :4639; apps/mobile/mobileLanClient.ts:452.

4 · Medium · Visible · Implementation

A single title lookup downloads the catalog

Problem. getLibraryItem calls getCanonicalItems, which requests both the library and series collections before searching locally. Index refresh also ignores the caller's ETag. Network traffic and JSON work grow with catalog size, even when a user opens only one title.

Why it matters. Use a dedicated detail request and retain a revision-aware catalog cache. Honor conditional refreshes and use pagination for collections. Measure transferred bytes and detail-open latency with a large library before claiming a speed improvement.

Evidence. apps/mobile/mobileLanClient.ts:240, :409 and :417.

5 · Medium · Inferred · Implementation

Folder changes can commit to only one store

Problem. The desktop add and remove handlers save their library mutation before awaiting the corresponding unified-server operation. There is no rollback in these handlers. If the second operation fails, the caller sees a failure after the local state has already changed.

Why it matters. Give one service ownership of folder mutations and derive other views from it. During migration, record pending synchronization and reconcile failures, or provide a compensating rollback. Verify add, remove and update with the second write forced to fail.

Evidence. apps/desktop/src/main/ipcHandlers.ts:751 and :782.

6 · Medium · Visible · Implementation

The main client files carry too many responsibilities

Problem. The mobile App file contains 6,824 lines and the desktop VideoPlayer contains 4,293. Mobile App includes connection recovery, credentials, artwork actions and rendering. Changes across these responsibilities are difficult to review and isolate.

Why it matters. Extract mobile connection and credential orchestration, catalog access, detail actions and player coordination into focused modules. Split the desktop player by engine adapter, playback session and controls. Keep shared contracts in packages, while preserving platform-specific behavior.

Evidence. line counts of apps/mobile/App.tsx and apps/desktop/src/components/VideoPlayer.tsx, excluding other files.

What is worth preserving

The repository already has typed IPC validation, trusted-sender checks, scoped permissions, hashed credentials, constrained media paths and shared protocol packages. These are useful engineering investments. Passing lint and type checks is also a good baseline, though neither establishes playback correctness.

Next actions

  1. Fix the viewer path disclosure and remove or restore the broken poster action.
  2. Make setup completion bounded and recoverable. Make folder synchronization failures explicit.
  3. Finish the canonical API migration, including detail requests, conditional catalog refreshes and server-driven capability checks.
  4. Refactor the two largest client files in small, behavior-preserving steps.
  5. Once runtime checks are requested, cover server restarts during playback, NAS disconnects, profile switches during pending writes, device revocation, subtitle changes, offline recovery and backup restoration.
  6. Review actual screens for keyboard and TV focus, screen-reader labels, text scaling, empty libraries and connection errors. These remain unverified here.
  7. Publish a platform capability matrix that distinguishes shipped behavior from incomplete work, and keep setup documentation and screenshots aligned with each release.
